title: AuroraCloud - Redwood marketplace integration tech sync
summary: Technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing, reference architecture, and joint solution for AuroraCloud customers. Covered listing checklist, VPC/private deployment options, RBAC/KMS requirements, and a plan for pilot benchmarks. Agreed next steps around RA draft, compliance docs, and a follow-up pilot window.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, AE on the partner program, Diego and Priya are with me on the tech side.
00:00:08 - Lina Chen: Thanks Maya, hi all, Lina here, we'll run through the agenda we shared.
00:00:15 - Rajiv Menon: hey, Rajiv joining from Aurora infra.
00:00:18 - Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, marketplace lead. Good to be here.
00:00:25 - Maya Patel: great, so quick agenda - listing readiness, reference arch, requirements for private / vpc and then pilot benchmarks, is that right?
00:00:34 - Lina Chen: yep that's perfect.
00:00:40 - Diego Ramos: just to set expectations, we'll walk through a recommended reference architecture for a Redwood hosted + dedicated hybrid on Aurora infra, show some rough perf/cost tradeoffs and note the assets we need from you for the marketplace listing.
00:00:55 - Rajiv Menon: sounds good. On the infra side we have managed GPU pools in our cloud regions and we can offer marketplace customers a managed deployment experience.
00:01:05 - Maya Patel: awesome. Quick question: is the plan to offer Redwood as a one-click marketplace listing that provisions into Aurora's managed cluster, or is this a bring-you-own-key / private control plane flow?
00:01:18 - Sofia Alvarez: our preference is one-click provisioning for most customers, but we need SSO and KMS integration for enterprise customers, and a private VPC option for regulated customers.
00:01:29 - Priya Kapoor: ok so we should map two flows: 1) marketplace managed deployment where Aurora provisions a dedicated Redwood instance, and 2) private deployment that points to customer-managed VPC or on-prem. The RA will show both.
00:01:45 - Lina Chen: can you call out what we need for the listing copy and the marketplace tile?
00:01:50 - Maya Patel: yes - we'll send a marketplace checklist: logo, short description, typical instance types (e.g., a2/g5 equivalence), quoting guidance, and a reference arch diagram. We'll also include a sample SLA and pricing guidance for dedicated capacity.
00:02:04 - Rajiv Menon: on networking - for the private VPC path we will need the control-plane to be reachable over a customer VPC peering or transit gateway, and we need your docs on required ports and CIDR ranges.
00:02:17 - Diego Ramos: noted, Rajiv. We'll produce a VPC diagram and a ports/egress table. Also, heads up - our runtime uses persistent KV cache and a few high-throughput ports for model shard fetch; some of our kernel-accelerated transports open ephemeral ranges. We can map that in the doc but our initial note: allow outbound to our model registry and optionally to S3 endpoints.
00:02:37 - Rajiv Menon: ok that last bit is important - if you fetch models from public registries we need to know which endpoints for firewall rules.
00:02:42 - Maya Patel: yes, we'll list registry endpoints, and for on-prem we have a model bundle option so nothing leaves the network.
00:02:50 - Sofia Alvarez: security question - SOC 2 and data residency are frequently asked by our enterprise customers. Where are Redwood's logs retained and how granular are audit logs?
00:02:59 - Priya Kapoor: we retain audit logs per account; we can configure retention windows (30/90/365 days) depending on the package. Our Private offering can forward logs to customer SIEM via syslog or Kinesis. We support KMS-backed encryption for model artifacts and in-flight TLS.
00:03:16 - Lina Chen: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) / HSM?
00:03:20 - Diego Ramos: yes, BYOK via AWS KMS or an HSM integration for on-prem. There may be a few config steps in the RA to wire the key policies.
00:03:28 - Rajiv Menon: great, that helps. For marketplace we'd like to show clear security badges on the listing; can you provide a compliance pack?
00:03:35 - Maya Patel: we will share the SOC2 summary and a compliance FAQ. Also we can provide an RD for customers that need ISO certs - we have cloud-region specific notes.
00:03:46 - Sofia Alvarez: perfect. Now, on performance: what's the recommended approach for low-latency interactive apps? Our customers often ask latency under 200ms for short responses.
00:03:57 - Priya Kapoor: low-latency is usually best on dedicated GPU pools with pre-warmed KV cache and small batching. For really strict p95 SLAs, the recommendation is pinned instances with warmed caches; for a more cost-sensitive workload we suggest autoscaling pods with prefix cache and a model variant that's quantized for throughput.
00:04:18 - Rajiv Menon: any specific numbers you can share for typical LLM config?
00:04:22 - Diego Ramos: rough numbers - on an a2-equivalent 80GB GPU, for a medium-sized model at 512 tokens AI, 1-2 tokens per ms for generation is typical in our tests but there's variance. We'll share benchmark spreadsheet, but it's important to pilot with your real workload.
00:04:39 - Lina Chen: yes pilot is key. timeline-wise, we want a pilot for a small set of customers in Q2, ideally a week-long smoke test and then a two-week benchmark. Is that feasible?
00:04:50 - Maya Patel: yes we can support a pilot. Diego, Priya: what do we need to run initial benchmarks on Aurora test infra?
00:04:58 - Diego Ramos: access to an Aurora staging cluster with the GPU profiles you plan to expose, sample prompts and token distributions, and network topology. Also, an account with metrics ingestion (prometheus or similar) so we can capture p95/p99 and token throughput.
00:05:10 - Rajiv Menon: we can provide a staging cluster and a prometheus endpoint. I'll upload sample workload traces.
00:05:16 - Sofia Alvarez: for the marketplace tile we'll need a few screenshots and a short demo video; can Redwood supply a short demo we can brand?
00:05:23 - Maya Patel: yes we'll send a 2-minute demo video and a quickstart doc.
00:05:28 - Lina Chen: can we talk about pricing callouts - should we show seat pricing or committed capacity for dedicated?
00:05:34 - Maya Patel: typically marketplace shows committed capacity options with a per-instance monthly price and an on-demand/hosted API price as an alternative. We'll share recommended price buckets that map to Aurora instance types.
00:05:45 - Priya Kapoor: also note that cost optimizations like batching and quantization can reduce unit cost substantially; we can add a small section in the RA about expected unit economics.
00:05:55 - Rajiv Menon: let's make sure we capture some known limitations - e.g., long-context models may not fit certain GPUs without sharding.
00:06:02 - Diego Ramos: correct, long context models will require sharding or sequence-parallel execution paths; we'll include a compatibility matrix in the RA.
00:06:10 - Lina Chen: any legal/procurement blockers for the listing?
00:06:14 - Maya Patel: procurement-wise we need a marketplace partner contract and an SLA attachment for dedicated purchases. We'll loop in legal but we can share a template.
00:06:22 - Sofia Alvarez: ok good. Action items recap, please?
00:06:26 - Maya Patel: sure. We'll send a RA first draft, the marketplace checklist, and a SOC2 summary. Aurora to send VPC diagram, prometheus endpoint, and sample workloads. Diego will run an initial benchmark once staging is ready.
00:06:39 - Rajiv Menon: we'll try to share the artifacts by end of week.
00:06:43 - Maya Patel: perfect. Any other questions?
00:06:46 - Lina Chen: just one - for the one-click provisioning, do you do operator-based installs or will you provide a marketplace AMI/container?
00:06:54 - Priya Kapoor: for Aurora-managed we recommend an operator + helm chart approach that provisions Redwood runtime into a namespaced deployment; for fully managed instances we can also provide a pre-baked container image and a terraform module. We'll include both options in the RA.
00:07:08 - Sofia Alvarez: ok that gives our product team enough to prototype the tile.
00:07:12 - Maya Patel: awesome, thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the benchmark kickoff for next week if your staging is ready.
00:07:20 - Rajiv Menon: thanks everyone.
00:07:23 - (end of recorded portion)

Notes: transcription includes some mis-heard terms (e.g., "K-V cash" in one segment), occasional speaker attribution errors expected. References: marketplace checklist doc link: https://redwood.ai/docs/marketplace-checklist, RA draft link: https://redwood.ai/internal/ra-drafts/auroracloud, benchmark spreadsheet link: https://redwood.ai/shared/benchmarks/aurora-pilot.
